title: Client-side merge heuristics and metering normalization for multipart delta replays
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Mobile and edge clients send delta updates (patch-like multipart fragments) when editing conversation state or documents. Due to lossy networks, clients sometimes retry or replay partial deltas, re-order fragments, or compress them using different client-side tokenization semantics. Current server-side metering credits every received fragment conservatively, leading to duplicate charges and skewed quota usage for customers. This ticket formalizes a heuristic-driven normalization layer that canonicalizes client multipart deltas before token counting and credits, minimizing duplicate charges while preserving correctness under replay and partial-merge scenarios.
background: We see recurring customer complaints about unexpectedly large token bills correlated to mobile editing flows. Telemetry shows a small percentage of sessions produce multiple partial replays with overlapping content. Existing related work: ENG-271234 suffix-trim, ENG-301919 interleaved-chat-edits (related symptoms but different approach). This ticket focuses on canonicalization and idempotency markers at the metering pipeline boundary, not on client SDK changes.
acceptance_criteria: Server applies canonical merge for multipart delta sequences and produces deterministic token counts for the same logical intent across replay scenarios
Duplicate or overlapping fragments from retries are detected and deduplicated in accounting within a 5s replay window by default
No more than 5% variance in token counts between canonicalized server-side approach and a gold-standard offline reassembly for synthetic test corpus
Unit and integration tests cover: out-of-order fragments, idempotent replays, compressed client tokenization variants, and partial aborts
Telemetry: new metric (metering.canonicalization_applied) and a dashboard to surface reductions in duplicate credits per session
design_decisions: Canonicalization happens in metering pre-processor before tokenizer invocation to avoid client-specific tokenization drift
We will use a lightweight fragment fingerprint: (session_id, logical_patch_id if present, fragment_offset, hash(fragment_payload)) to detect overlapping content
Introduce a soft replay window (configurable, default 5s) per session for dedupe. Outside the window we conservatively charge to avoid under-billing long-tail replays
If client provides an idempotency token or logical_patch_id we prefer it; otherwise we fall back to fingerprint heuristics
For compressed multipart payloads (client-side zlib/gzip), we rehydrate before canonicalization; if rehydration fails we fallback to payload-length-based heuristics and mark as partial_credit
We will not change upstream billing ledger schema; we add a canonicalization flag to per-charge metadata for audit and potential retro-crediting
implementation_notes: Add a MeteringPreprocessor component into ingestion path (stateless, runs on request node)

Preprocessor responsibilities: normalize fragment order, merge contiguous offsets, detect overlaps, emit canonicalized payloads for tokenizer, and annotate metering records with canonicalization_applied=true/false
Store short-lived fragment anchors in a bounded LRU per-session cache (TTL = replay_window) to detect duplicates without a distributed store
For interleaved multi-tenant proxying, ensure fragment cache keys are namespaced by tenant and session to avoid cross-tenant bleed
Add feature flag to toggle canonicalization and to control replay_window in runtime config for experimentation
test_plan: Unit tests: fragment fingerprint collisions, partial rehydrate failover, canonical merge correctness for synthetic fragments
Integration tests: end-to-end request -> canonicalized token count -> ledger entry comparison against offline assembler
Fuzz tests: random fragment order/replay patterns up to 50 fragments/session to validate idempotency and memory bounds
Load test: synthetic mobile workload with 10k concurrent sessions to observe latency p95 impact of preprocessor
Billing regression test: run historical 7-day sample traffic through canonicalizer and assert 95th percentile of per-session bill delta <= 10% (we expect large reductions for pathological sessions)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable canonicalization for 1% of mobile sessions behind feature flag and collect metering.canonicalization_applied, token_delta, and latency per-request
Phase 2 (ramp): 10% -> 50% over 2 weeks while validating no customer-impacting undercharges; run reconciliation job against audited ledger
Phase 3 (global): Enable by default with gradual ramp to 100% and create internal retro-crediting path for obvious double-charged sessions caught during canary
Rollback: feature flag off and replay original fragments into legacy pipeline to reconstitute previous charge amounts if we detect systemic under-billing
